cards.power: The Hepcidin Lock. During inflammation, Ian is locked in the warehouse so Bacteria Pirates can't steal him.
cards.lore: Low Ferritin = Ian is broke. High Ferritin + Low TIBC = Ian is hoarding during chronic disease.
cards.gradeReason: Hoarding iron during inflammation — vivid, but hepcidin context needed to fully perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Armadillo locked in gold cage, bulldog guard with key, bacteria pirates outside. Style: MedKayfab punk. Mood: Guarded fortress.

cards.power: The Megaloblastic Glitch. DNA fails to replicate, so they just grow fat without dividing.
cards.lore: Bill needs his VIP pass to enter the Terminal Ileum. No Bill = Nerve Damage. Phil is just a leafy-green local.
cards.gradeReason: VIP pass for intrinsic factor is instant. Growing fat without dividing — players perform immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Two enormous walruses wedged in doorway labeled Cell Cycle, VIP badge on one. Style: MedKayfab slapstick. Mood: Bloated and blocked.

cards.power: The Vaso-Occlusive Jam. Under stress (cold, acid, low O2), Sam stiffens into a blade and clogs the highway.
cards.lore: Protects against Malaria (The Parasite Tax) but shreds the Spleen (Autosplenectomy) by age 10.
cards.gradeReason: Stiffens into a blade and clogs the highway — visceral instant embodiment. Parasite Tax seals it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Sickle-shaped red cell blocking blood vessel highway in icy storm. Style: MedKayfab action. Mood: Cold and locked.

cards.power: The Globin Imbalance. Missing chains make the hemoglobin lopsided and highly fragile.
cards.lore: Crew-cut skull X-ray because his bone marrow is working overtime to fix the mess.
cards.gradeReason: Lopsided gorilla with uneven barbell — clear image, needs alpha/beta chain context to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Gorilla lifting unbalanced barbell labeled Alpha/Beta, skull with crew-cut X-ray. Style: MedKayfab strongman. Mood: Strained imbalance.

cards.power: The Fava Bean Trigger. Without his shield, Pete gets roasted by oxidative stress and sulfa-bombs.
cards.lore: X-linked. The Spleen-Bouncer bites out the oxidized junk (Heinz bodies), leaving bite cells.
cards.gradeReason: Roasted without his shield is vivid, but the shield-absence mechanic needs a beat of context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Hedgehog with cracked NADPH shield fleeing fava bean explosion, Spleen-Bouncer biting behind. Style: MedKayfab peril. Mood: Exposed and burning.

cards.power: The Spleen Bait. Sid has no skeleton. The spleen despises perfect circles and destroys them.
cards.lore: High MCHC is the giveaway—he is packed too tight!
cards.gradeReason: The spleen despises perfect circles — pure invitation. Sid walks to his doom and players feel it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Inflated pufferfish trembling before grinning shark labeled Spleen. Style: MedKayfab horror-comedy. Mood: Doomed perfection.

cards.power: The Midnight Hit. Without his anchor, the Complement hornets assume he's an intruder and pop him at night.
cards.lore: Look for the morning aftermath: dark urine from nighttime hemolysis.
cards.gradeReason: Complement hornets pop him at night — perfect nocturnal ambush. Morning aftermath clincher.
cards.artworkPrompt: Bat without anchor tag fleeing hornet complement swarm at midnight. Style: MedKayfab noir. Mood: Nocturnal terror.

cards.power: The Enzyme Choke. Larry jams up ALAD and Ferrochelatase, shutting down the heme factory.
cards.lore: Causes sideroblastic anemia; ringed sideroblasts form as iron gets stuck in the mitochondria waiting for heme.
cards.gradeReason: Jams the heme factory is solid industrial sabotage — two-enzyme block needs one beat of context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Beaver gnawing toxic green pipe, iron balls queued outside ring-shaped mitochondria. Style: MedKayfab industrial. Mood: Toxic blockade.

cards.power: The Hypoxic Scream. When O2 is low, Eric screams at the marrow to start mass-producing red cells.
cards.lore: If the kidneys fail, Eric dies, and the marrow sleeps (Anemia of Chronic Kidney Disease).
cards.gradeReason: Screams at marrow to mass-produce — zero ambiguity. Players scream on cue.
cards.artworkPrompt: Yellow monkey shrieking into megaphone at glowing bone-cave marrow. Style: MedKayfab urgent. Mood: Desperate oxygen alarm.

cards.power: The Marrow Metric. Rick is the raw recruit. If he's surging (>2%), the marrow is fighting the anemia.
cards.lore: If Rick is <1% during anemia, the marrow factory is broken or missing ingredients.
cards.gradeReason: Raw recruit surging vs. giving up — interpretable, but threshold numbers need a moment to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Golden retriever puppy sprinting in boxing ring, marrow factory smoking behind. Style: MedKayfab rookie. Mood: Eager but untested.

cards.power: The Cleanup Crew. Harry binds free hemoglobin to save the kidneys from toxic damage.
cards.lore: If Harry is entirely missing from the blood, it means there was a massive murder (hemolysis) and he used himself up cleaning the mess.
cards.gradeReason: Massive murder — he mopped himself out of existence. Instant crime-scene performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Raccoon janitor dissolving into bloodstained mop on pink-red floor. Style: MedKayfab noir. Mood: Sacrificial cleanup.

cards.power: The Tag Reader. Carl detects if the immune system has placed a hit-marker on the body's own cells.
cards.lore: Direct Coombs looks for antibodies ALREADY attached to the RBC.
cards.gradeReason: Tag reader detective is clear; already-attached antibody distinction needs one explanatory beat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Bloodhound detective magnifying biohazard stickers on sheep, glowing antibodies pre-attached. Style: MedKayfab investigative. Mood: Surveillance.

cards.cardName: The Agglutinin Sisters (Cold Chloe & Warm Wally)
cards.power: The Clump. Chloe clumps in the extremities (fingers/nose). Wally attacks at core body temperature.
cards.lore: Chloe = Mycoplasma (Walking Pneumonia). Wally = SLE or CLL.
cards.gradeReason: Two characters one card — clever, but cognitive split. Chloe/Wally need table setup to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Polar bear and sweating camel clumping red cells, hot-cold split sky behind them. Style: MedKayfab duality. Mood: Temperature warfare.

cards.power: The Factory Strike. A congenital defect where the red cell assembly line simply never opens.
cards.lore: Look for physical anomalies: triphalangeal or absent thumbs combined with pure red cell aplasia in an infant.
cards.gradeReason: Assembly line never opens — conceptually clear but more architectural than embodied performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Wide-eyed lemur staring into empty chest, vacant factory inside, absent thumb prominent. Style: MedKayfab congenital. Mood: Assembly line silence.

cards.power: The Left Shift. When the bacterial war gets too big, Ned calls in his unbaked teenage brothers (Bands) to fight.
cards.lore: Red dies fast and turns into pus. Without him, the body is a wide-open fortress.
cards.gradeReason: Unbaked teenage brothers called to war — players are in. Wide-open fortress seals the dread.
cards.artworkPrompt: SWAT badger leading gang of immature badger recruits against bacteria mob. Style: MedKayfab riot. Mood: Desperate reinforcements.

cards.power: The Toxic Granules. Eddie unleashes major basic protein to dissolve invaders too big to eat.
cards.lore: The star of the NAACP (Neoplasm, Allergy, Asthma, Collagen vascular disease, Parasites).
cards.gradeReason: Pink flamingo ninja dissolving parasites — instant role. NAACP mnemonic is a gift.
cards.artworkPrompt: Pink flamingo in black ninja suit slicing giant worm with katana, toxic pink spray. Style: MedKayfab assassin. Mood: Toxic elegance.

cards.power: The Hidden Trigger. Benny is incredibly rare; he dumps histamine to cause extreme vasodilation.
cards.lore: If Benny is elevated in the blood, DO NOT ignore it. Check for CML—he is often the hidden driver of the leukemia train.
cards.gradeReason: Hidden driver of the leukemia train is ominous — rarity makes role abstract until CML context lands.
cards.artworkPrompt: Glowing purple octopus lurking in dark blood vessel, histamine bombs detonating, CML train behind. Style: MedKayfab hidden. Mood: Rare menace.

cards.power: The Tissue Transformation. Monty cruises the blood, but when he enters tissue, he transforms into the ultimate garbage disposal.
cards.lore: He eats the debris Ned leaves behind and presents the evidence to the T-cells.
cards.gradeReason: Garbage disposal transformation on tissue entry is instant. Debris chain from Ned is perfect continuity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Turtle entering phone booth, T-rex macrophage exploding out the other side. Style: MedKayfab transformation. Mood: Slow then ferocious.

cards.power: Adaptive Memory. Lou doesn't just kill; he remembers. He holds the blueprints for lifelong immunity.
cards.lore: Viral infections (like EBV/Mono) cause Lou to morph into giant, atypical reactive lymphocytes.
cards.gradeReason: Remembers and holds blueprints — compelling but slightly broad for immediate single-turn performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Black panther sniper on rooftop with blueprint tattoos, fighting giant atypical lymphocyte clone. Style: MedKayfab special ops. Mood: Adaptive memory.

cards.power: The Marrow Wipeout. The stem cells are annihilated. RBCs, WBCs, and platelets all crash to zero.
cards.lore: Bone marrow biopsy yields a Dry Tap (nothing but fat). Triggered by radiation, drugs, or Parvovirus B19.
cards.gradeReason: All crash to zero, Dry Tap nothing but fat — emptiness is instantly embodied. Zero filler.
cards.artworkPrompt: Hermit crab emerging from hollow shell, nothing but fat cells inside. Style: MedKayfab emptiness. Mood: Total marrow void.

cards.power: The Fibrotic Squeeze. Max replaces the plush marrow with stiff collagen fibrosis.
cards.lore: Red blood cells must physically squeeze through the fibrotic stone to escape, permanently deforming into Teardrop Cells.
cards.gradeReason: Squeeze through fibrotic stone and emerge permanently deformed — visceral, no context needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Medusa creature turning red marrow to stone, teardrop cells squeezed through rocky cracks. Style: MedKayfab petrification. Mood: Stony squeeze.

cards.power: The Unstoppable Signal. Jake ignores the off-switch. He tells the marrow to divide forever.
cards.lore: The root villain behind the Myeloproliferative Wars: Polycythemia Vera, Essential Thrombocythemia, and Myelofibrosis.
cards.gradeReason: Ignores the off-switch, divides forever — classic villain energy, instant embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Spiked boar slamming glowing ON button, marrow factory producing endless cells. Style: MedKayfab villain. Mood: Unstoppable signal.

cards.power: The Viscous Sludge. Too many red cells turn the blood flow into thick, dangerous mud.
cards.lore: Patients get intensely itchy after a hot shower (aquagenic pruritus) due to mast cell degranulation.
cards.gradeReason: Blood turns to thick mud — instantly physical. Itchy shower pearl is unforgettable clinical detail.
cards.artworkPrompt: Bloated red bull soaking in bathtub of sludge, scratching furiously, steam rising. Style: MedKayfab bloat. Mood: Viscous misery.

cards.power: The Platelet Paradox. Toby makes massive amounts of dysfunctional platelets, causing simultaneous clotting and bleeding.
cards.lore: Diagnosis of exclusion. You must rule out reactive thrombocytosis (like iron deficiency or infection) first!
cards.gradeReason: Simultaneous clotting and bleeding clicks — but exclusion diagnosis requirement needs table framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Spider-surgeon with eight arms wielding clotting tools and scissors, bleeding everywhere simultaneously. Style: MedKayfab paradox. Mood: Chaotic overproduction.

cards.power: The Pre-Leukemic Limbo. The marrow makes cells, but they are ugly, mutated, and die before leaving the factory.
cards.lore: High risk of transforming directly into Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML).
cards.gradeReason: Ugly cells die at factory gates — vivid, but AML transformation risk needs one framing beat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Platypus in broken lab coat surrounded by mutated cell splatter, AML shadow looming. Style: MedKayfab pre-leukemic. Mood: Factory floor chaos.

cards.power: The Cytokine Storm. The immune system goes rogue, and macrophages begin eating the body's own healthy blood cells.
cards.lore: Ferritin levels explode into the tens of thousands as Hank rampages. A true hematologic emergency.
cards.gradeReason: Macrophages eating own blood cells, ferritin exploding — emergency felt immediately. Internal Cannibal is iconic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Neon crocodile devouring red and white cells, FERRITIN BOMB caption, extreme inflammation label. Style: MedKayfab emergency. Mood: Auto-cannibalistic rampage.

cards.power: The Lipid Trash Pile. Gary lacks the enzyme to break down lipids, so they accumulate inside macrophages.
cards.lore: Crinkled paper cytoplasm on biopsy. Severe hepatosplenomegaly and avascular necrosis of the femur.
cards.gradeReason: Crinkled paper cytoplasm is clinically iconic; enzyme-deficiency mechanism needs one beat of framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Rhinoceros with crinkled-paper skin sagging under lipid weight, femur bone cracking. Style: MedKayfab storage. Mood: Crumpling under accumulation.

cards.power: The Chemo-Recovery. Nate artificially stimulates the marrow to pump out new neutrophils.
cards.lore: Deployed after brutal chemotherapy regimens to pull the patient out of the neutropenic danger zone.
cards.gradeReason: Deployed after chemo to pump neutrophils — therapeutic role clear but less character than disease cards.
cards.artworkPrompt: Owl wizard raising ghost neutrophils from graveyard with glowing staff, badger army summoned. Style: MedKayfab recovery. Mood: Marrow resurrection.

cards.power: The Origin Seed. Every single cell in the hematology universe starts by passing his check.
cards.lore: Target CD34+ cells for bone marrow transplants—they are the blank slates that rebuild the system.
cards.gradeReason: Every cell passes his check — foundational but abstract until transplant context clarifies the stakes.
cards.artworkPrompt: Massive gorilla bouncer at velvet rope outside Peripheral Blood nightclub, cell lineup queuing. Style: MedKayfab exclusive. Mood: Origin checkpoint.

cards.power: The Platelet Bridge. Vinny connects platelets to the exposed collagen of a broken vessel wall.
cards.lore: Most common inherited bleeding disorder. Vinny also carries Factor VIII on his back to keep it from degrading.
cards.gradeReason: Carries Factor VIII on his back — dual role is instantly playable. The Glue bridges everything.
cards.artworkPrompt: Green lizard gluing platelets to broken pipe wall, Factor VIII barrel strapped to back. Style: MedKayfab repair. Mood: Essential adhesive.

cards.power: The Sticky Failure. Ben's platelets are huge, but they lack the receptor to grab Vinny's glue.
cards.lore: Ristocetin test shows NO clumping. Unlike VWD, adding normal plasma does not fix Ben.
cards.gradeReason: Can't grab Vinny's glue — elegant cross-card reference but needs VWD comparison to fully perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: T-rex with huge malfunctioning arms failing to grab glue bottle, giant platelets scattered. Style: MedKayfab failure. Mood: Huge but helpless.

cards.power: The Aggregation Block. Glenn has no handshakes, so platelets can stick to the wall, but CANNOT stick to each other.
cards.lore: Bleeding time is prolonged, but platelet count is completely normal.
cards.gradeReason: No handshakes so platelets can't aggregate — the mechanic IS the performance. Perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Penguin colony with bandaged arms unable to clasp each other, vessel wall intact behind. Style: MedKayfab aggregation. Mood: Isolated islands.

cards.power: The Anti-Platelet Hit. IgG antibodies mark platelets for death, and the spleen executes them.
cards.lore: The marrow responds by pumping out massive Megakaryocytes trying to replace the losses.
cards.gradeReason: Marked for death and the spleen executes them — murder procedural in one line. G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Hyena pack chasing glowing marked platelets toward spleen execution chamber. Style: MedKayfab hit-squad. Mood: Platelet massacre.

cards.power: The Micro-Clot Storm. Huge vWF multimers don't get chopped up, acting like massive spiderwebs that shred passing red cells (Schistocytes).
cards.lore: Remember FAT RK: Fever, Anemia (MAHA), Thrombocytopenia, Renal, Neuro symptoms.
cards.gradeReason: FAT RK mnemonic is gold; vWF spiderweb mechanism vivid but ADAMTS13 bridge needs one beat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Five-headed red dragon with missing sword labeled ADAMTS13, red cells shredded in web-clot storm. Style: MedKayfab multi-threat. Mood: Terrible cascade.

cards.power: The Toxin Shredder. Similar microthrombi to TTP, but triggered by undercooked meat toxins.
cards.lore: Typically hits children. Dominant symptoms are renal failure and bloody diarrhea; skips the neuro symptoms of TTP.
cards.gradeReason: Undercooked meat toxin shredder is vivid — TTP distinction by renal-not-neuro needs one beat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Skunk spraying shiga-toxin green at kidney, bloody diarrhea burger in background. Style: MedKayfab food-horror. Mood: Gut-to-kidney toxin.

cards.power: The Paradox. The coagulation cascade fires everywhere at once, consuming all factors, resulting in massive bleeding elsewhere.
cards.lore: Sepsis, trauma, or obstetrical complications. PT and PTT are both elevated.
cards.gradeReason: Cascade fires everywhere consuming all factors — the paradox is the performance. Instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Two entwined snakes clotting and bleeding simultaneously, PARADOX label, sepsis explosion. Style: MedKayfab paradox. Mood: Catastrophic consumption.

cards.power: The Intrinsic Break. The intrinsic cascade fails, preventing a solid secondary hemostatic plug.
cards.lore: X-linked recessive. Hallmark symptom is Hemarthrosis (deep bleeding into the joints). PT is normal!
cards.gradeReason: Deep joint bleeds, PT normal — clinically critical, instantly memorable. Royal Bleeder nails the role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Crowned swan bleeding into joints, crown askew, PT=NORMAL scrawled in corner. Style: MedKayfab royal tragedy. Mood: Hemarthrosis nobility.

cards.power: The Spark. Sam triggers the entire clotting cascade the moment tissue damage exposes him to the blood.
cards.lore: He has the shortest half-life of all the factors. When Vitamin K drops, Sam is the first to die (PT rises first).
cards.gradeReason: First to die when Vitamin K drops — shortest half-life is a perfect clinical death sentence.
cards.artworkPrompt: Bald eagle on Tissue Factor perch holding stopwatch, Vitamin K candle burning very short. Style: MedKayfab monarch. Mood: Brief but decisive spark.

cards.power: The Convergence. Whether the alarm was Intrinsic or Extrinsic, they all meet at Factor X to finish the job.
cards.lore: If the Common Pathway is broken, BOTH the PT and PTT times will be elevated.
cards.gradeReason: Convergence point is structurally clear but more mechanism than character — needs table framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Kangaroo at PT/PTT crossroads, both roads converging at Factor X finish line. Style: MedKayfab convergence. Mood: All roads meet here.

cards.power: The Activator. The factors are useless, unarmed thugs until Kevin adds a carboxyl group so they can bind to calcium.
cards.lore: Neonates lack gut bacteria to make Kevin, which is why they get a Vitamin K shot at birth.
cards.gradeReason: Unarmed thugs activated by the mob boss — players are in immediately. Neonatal shot is gold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Bulldog mob boss in pinstripe suit distributing carboxyl weapons to factor gang. Style: MedKayfab organized crime. Mood: Factorial authority.

cards.power: The Epoxide Saboteur. Warrick halts the recycling of Vitamin K, slowly starving the cascade of active factors.
cards.lore: Because Protein C (the brake) drops first, Warrick causes a transient hypercoagulable state. Bridge with Heparin!
cards.gradeReason: Starving the cascade is immediate saboteur energy. Protein C brake dropping first is a clinical gem.
cards.artworkPrompt: Weasel pouring acid into Vitamin K recycling drum, Kevin the mob boss visibly weakening. Style: MedKayfab sabotage. Mood: Slow starvation.

cards.power: The Immediate Halt. Hep binds to AT-III, instantly neutralizing Thrombin and Factor Xa.
cards.lore: Reversal agent is Protamine Sulfate. Watch out for HIT (Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia).
cards.gradeReason: Immediate halt via AT-III is mechanism-forward; HIT warning elevates clinical urgency to solid G2.
cards.artworkPrompt: Armored rhino with Antithrombin III shield electrifying incoming thrombin, HIT warning caption. Style: MedKayfab halt. Mood: Instant neutralization.

cards.power: The Regulatory Stop. They ensure a clot doesn't keep growing until it blocks the entire blood vessel.
cards.lore: Deficiency means the patient is chronically hypercoagulable (prone to DVTs at a young age).
cards.gradeReason: Regulatory brakes are clear; functional description stays slightly above character-level performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Two cheetahs racing to smash STOP-V and STOP-VIII buttons at clotting cascade factory. Style: MedKayfab regulation. Mood: Racing to brake.

cards.power: The Mutant Immunity. Factor V is mutated so that Protein C physically cannot cleave it. The brakes are broken.
cards.lore: The clotting cascade stays ON. Suspect in young, healthy patients presenting with unprovoked DVTs/PEs.
cards.gradeReason: The brakes are broken — three words, zero ambiguity. Unstoppable is exactly what players embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Armored boar immune to cheetah claws, clotting cascade ON forever, DVT trail behind. Style: MedKayfab mutant villain. Mood: Uncleavable menace.

cards.power: The Universal Betrayal. O is the universal donor; AB is the universal recipient. Cross him, and you die.
cards.lore: Giving the wrong ABO type causes acute hemolytic transfusion reaction (preformed IgM antibodies attack instantly).
cards.gradeReason: Cross him and you die — four words, highest stakes. Players feel the weight immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Bear with blood type tornado, A/B/AB/O bags spinning, preformed IgM missiles launching. Style: MedKayfab transfusion. Mood: Cross-match death sentence.

cards.power: The Second Baby Trap. Sensitization happens during the first birth. The antibodies wait to attack the next Rh(+) pregnancy.
cards.lore: Give RhoGAM at 28 weeks and postpartum to hide the Rh(+) signal and prevent sensitization.
cards.gradeReason: Antibodies wait for the second pregnancy — the trap is the performance. Rhonda's timeline is felt.
cards.artworkPrompt: Armored kangaroo mother with spiked pouch, second baby targeted by antibody missiles. Style: MedKayfab maternal. Mood: Second pregnancy ambush.

cards.power: The White-Out. Donor antibodies attack the recipient's neutrophils in the pulmonary capillaries, flooding the lungs with fluid.
cards.lore: Non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema occurring within 6 hours of a transfusion.
cards.gradeReason: Lungs flooding within 6 hours — clinical urgency vivid but mechanism slightly explanatory over performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Pufferfish X-ray exploding in lung capillaries, donor antibodies attacking neutrophils, white-out flood. Style: MedKayfab pulmonary. Mood: Drowning white-out.

cards.power: Pushing too much blood volume too fast overwhelms a weak heart.
cards.lore: Unlike TRALI, TACO presents with high blood pressure, JVD, and high BNP. Treat with diuretics.
cards.gradeReason: No named Power title — purely descriptive. TRALI distinction useful but card is the deck's weakest.
cards.artworkPrompt: Pelican pouring water into overflowing hospital bed, heart buckling, JVD neck veins visible. Style: MedKayfab overload. Mood: Cardiovascular flood.

cards.power: The Quality Control. He removes inclusions (Howell-Jolly bodies) and destroys antibody-coated cells.
cards.lore: If removed, patients are fatally susceptible to encapsulated Ninja bacteria (Strep pneumo, Neisseria, H. flu). Vaccinate!
cards.gradeReason: Encapsulated Ninja bacteria waiting for the spleen to leave — clinical pearl IS the performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Muscular frog bouncer on red cell highway flicking out Howell-Jolly debris, ninja bacteria lurking. Style: MedKayfab bouncer. Mood: Vigilant quality control.

cards.power: The Hard Set. Thrombin cleaves Fred into Fibrin, turning the temporary platelet plug into a concrete wall.
cards.lore: Without Fred, the clot dissolves under blood pressure.
cards.gradeReason: Concrete wall from platelet putty — the upgrade is instant. Without Fred it dissolves: clear stakes.
cards.artworkPrompt: Giant spider weaving fibrin ropes around platelet crowd, concrete wall forming behind. Style: MedKayfab hard-set. Mood: Permanent sealing.

cards.power: The Demolition. When activated by tPA, Pam becomes Plasmin and digests the fibrin clot to restore blood flow.
cards.lore: Administered clinically (tPA) for acute ischemic strokes, but contra-indicated if the patient is bleeding!
cards.gradeReason: Demolition via tPA activation is mechanistic; contra-indication warning is the critical clinical beat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Toucan with scissors beak cutting fibrin ropes, tPA syringe in wing, bleeding warning sign. Style: MedKayfab demolition. Mood: Clot excavation.

cards.power: The Breadcrumb Trail. Dan only exists if a massive clot was formed AND broken down.
cards.lore: Highly sensitive, not specific. A negative D-Dimer rules out a Pulmonary Embolism, but a positive one doesn't confirm it.
cards.gradeReason: Breadcrumb only exists after clot plus breakdown — elegant two-step logic needs a beat to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Bloodhound detective with UV light finding glowing fibrin crumbs, PE shadow in background. Style: MedKayfab forensic. Mood: Sensitive but nonspecific.

verdict: Fifty-two characters, zero throwaways — this is the complete hematology roster from iron metabolism to DIC and back again. PNH-Paul's Complement hornets, Haptoglobin Harry mopping himself out of existence, ABO-Arthur's four-word death sentence: these are G1 performances the table will never forget. The one weak link is TACO-Tom, who shows up without a named Power title in a deck where every other card has one — sticks out like a cold agglutinin at the equator. TTP-Terry's stat box also has a typo: ADANTS13 instead of ADAMTS13 — fix before Gumroad. Table-ready: YES, with two surgical edits.
blurb: The complete hematology cast — from iron metabolism to coagulation disorders to transfusion reactions — built for medical students who need to remember everything before the shelf exam. Fifty-two characters, zero filler.

marketingText:
MedKayfab: HEMATOLOGY – The Bloodline Feuds (Medical Mnemonics Cut & Play Comic)

56 illustrated medical mnemonic cards to master the hemolytic anemias, the coagulation cascade and the bleeders that break it, and the bone-marrow malignancies that crowd the healthy lines out.

Here is how a clot actually decides to form. One factor nicks the next, that one wakes the factor after it, and a single small insult amplifies down the chain until a mesh of fibrin locks the breach. Run the same cascade a hair too eagerly and the mesh forms where no wound exists. Strip out its brakes and the patient bleeds into a joint from the act of standing up. Hematology is the specialty where nothing screams and everything is a chain reaction you cannot see with your eyes.

MedKayfab Hematology turns the blood, the marrow, and the clotting cascade into a narrative wrestling match. The numbers on the count are not the fight; they are the scoreboard. You learn each cell line and each factor by its face, so when a smear or a coagulation panel comes back wrong, you already know which feud broke out and who threw the first punch.

YOU'LL GET
- 56 illustrated MedKayfab cards (14pp, 4 cards/page)
- Full MedKayfab Freestyle rules (Quest Die mechanics)
- S-Tier characters like TTP-Terry, Sickle-Sam, and Haptoglobin Harry
- Free lifetime updates as guidelines evolve
- CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence, print, share, and adapt freely
- PDF optimized for home printing (A4 / Letter)

What's in the deck
This deck personifies the Flow layer of medicine, the cells and factors that have to keep moving or the whole body stalls. You'll meet TTP-Terry, who loses the referee that keeps von Willebrand strings in line and lets micro-clots shred every red cell that tries to squeeze past. You'll meet Sickle-Sam, the cell that turns rigid and crescent the moment oxygen runs low, jamming the very capillaries he was built to glide through. And you'll meet Haptoglobin Harry, the clean-up man whose absence is the tell: when Harry has vanished from the panel, red cells are bursting inside the vessels and the body has run out of mops. From the marrow feuds of Myelofibrosis Max to the missing-factor bleeds of Von Willebrand Vinny, the deck covers the full bloodline.

How it works
Every card is a cognitive anchor built for high-stress retrieval. You have the Character (the mnemonic), the Visual (the scene), the Stat Block (the counts, the markers, the cutoffs), the Lore (the clinical story), and the Quest (the reasoning challenge). The Mechanism Flash mode is unforgiving here: if you cannot explain, in one sentence and without looking, why TTP eats platelets while DIC eats everything, the "patient" on the Stage doesn't make it to the next round.

Honest cognitive load
This is an A-Tier deck with a lot of moving parts, best suited to medical students in their clinical years and residents in internal medicine or hematology-oncology. It pairs naturally with Immunology & Pathology for the hemolysis and marrow mechanisms underneath the characters, with Laboratory Medicine for the smear and panel reading the Quests demand, and with Oncology when the bloodline feuds tip over into leukemia and lymphoma.

ABOUT MEDKAYFAB
MedKayfab is a narrative medical learning card game, 50 decks covering the full medical curriculum. Every card encodes a clinical mechanism as a character with a personality, a story, and a reasoning challenge. Built by a physician. Assembled with AI tools. Manually revised. Honest about its limitations. Free to use, share, and adapt under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
